title: Classical Arabic Grammar
subtitle: Integrated 26-Week Curriculum in Ṣarf, Naḥw, and Iʿrāb

referenceEditions.title: A New Arabic Grammar of the Written Language
A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic

scope.focus: Classical Arabic, Qur'anic syntax, morphology (ṣarf), syntax (naḥw), grammatical inflection (iʿrāb), and classical-text reading.
excluded: Modern conversational, journalistic, or spoken dialect lessons
methodologicalPrinciples: Primary dual discipline: Morphology (ṣarf) for root derivation and metric paradigms (wazn), paired with Syntax & Inflection (naḥw / iʿrāb) for syntactic governance (ʿamal).
Full desinential inflection (iʿrāb): vocalize every case and mood ending (ḍammah, fatḥah, kasrah, sukūn) to preserve grammatical meaning.
Original instructional content: explanations and exercises are authored originally for this app, using Haywood & Nahmad and Ryding as syllabus and theoretical references.
irabRoutine: Sentence Boundary & Type: Identify whether the clause is Nominal (Ismiyyah) or Verbal (Fiʿliyyah).
Isolate Nuclear Components: Mubtadaʾ + Khabar (with kāna/inna if present), or Fiʿl + Fāʿil + Mafʿūl Bihi.
Account for Governing Agents (ʿAwāmil): Check mood particles (nawāṣib, jawāzim) and case governors (prepositions, iḍāfah, ḥāl, tamyīz, illā).

conventions.transliteration: Academic Latin transliteration with macrons (ā, ī, ū), underdots (ḥ, ṣ, ḍ, ṭ, ẓ), hamza (ʾ), and ʿayn (ʿ). Arabic script with full tashkīl remains primary.
conventions.chapterOrderNote: Haywood & Nahmad Chapters 1–52 + Literary Supplement are mapped across 26 weeks alongside Karin C. Ryding Chapters 1–39 & Appendices I–II. Original textbook chapter numbers are preserved.

modules.title: Foundational Classical Morphology & Nominal Syntax
modules.summary: Script, phonetics, nominal sentences, the 3-case system, annexation (iḍāfah), personal/demonstrative pronouns, adjectives, Form I perfect verbs, and Week 8 consolidation.
modules.checkpoint: Read aloud and parse the iʿrāb of unvocalized nominal and verbal sentences, naming every case ending and governing factor (ʿāmil).

modules.title: The Classical Verbal System, Mood Governance & Morphological Stems
modules.chapterRange: Haywood Ch. 14–31, 33 · Ryding Ch. 2, 20–32, 34–35, 38, App. I
modules.summary: Imperfect moods (Indicative, Subjunctive, Jussive), Imperative, Passive Voice, Derived Forms II–X, doubled/hamzated/weak verbs, lexicography, and Week 17 consolidation.
modules.checkpoint: Conjugate across all derived and weak paradigms, explain mood governance, and extract underlying roots for classical dictionary lookup.

modules.title: Advanced Classical Syntax, Qur'anic Structures & Textual Iʿrāb
modules.chapterRange: Haywood Ch. 32, 34–52 & Supplement · Ryding Ch. 5–6, 8–11, 14–16, 18–19, 36–37, 39, App. II
modules.summary: Particles of praise/blame, relative and conditional clauses, numerals, noun derivations, comprehensive accusative syntax, diptotes, classical metrics, and authentic literary analysis.
modules.checkpoint: Execute full word-by-word iʿrāb on Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, classical hadith, Kalīlah wa-Dimnah, and Ibn Baṭṭūṭah.
